Wrapping Cloudflare workers and third-party AI and non-AI APIs endpoints with key authentication

This demo will try to:

- Enable `api.raunaqgupta.com`
- Expose various single-function cloudflare workers under the `/utilities` path.
- Expose my aqicn.org API token protected endpoint under the `/aqi` path without exposing the token.
- Enable key authentication on all endpoints.
- Expose a basic single-response AI endpoint under the `/ai` path.

## Enable the `api` sub-domain

- Kong Konnect's free tier provides one free API gateway.
- Provisioned API gateway can be configured for a non-apex domain.

## Expose a datetime utility under `/utilities`

- Created a Cloudflare worker to return the current date and time in JSON format with an optional `timezone` query parameter.
- Setup route on Kong Konnect's API gateway to redirect to `/utilities/datetime`.

```sh
curl -X GET "https://api.raunaqgupta.com/utilities/datetime?timezone=PST"
```

```sh
{
  "timezone": "PST",
  "timestamp": "Monday, January 12, 2026 at 5:10:09 PM PST",
  "iso": "2026-01-13T01:10:09.391Z"
}                                                                                                                                                                     
```

## Expose an air quality index endpoint under `/aqi`

- Exposed aqicn.org's `feed` endpoint at `api.raunaqgupta.com/aqi/feed/:city` without requiring to expose the API token. This endpoint takes a city name as a parameter and returns the air quality index data for that city in JSON format.
- Use Kong Konnect's API gateway to route requests to `https://api.waqi.info/feed/:city/?token=YOUR_API_TOKEN`.
- Utilize the `Request Transformer Advanced` plugin to store the personal API token in the gateway instead of exposing it on the client side.

### Notes

- Kong Konnect lets you use the Konnect vault in the `Request Transformer Advanced` plugin even though it's not supported. Both copilot chat and documentation confirm this: https://developer.konghq.com/how-to/configure-the-konnect-config-store/#can-i-reference-konnect-config-store-vault-secrets-in-kong-conf

## STAR methodology

S – Situation: A description of the circumstance leading up to the skill being demonstrated. Don’t give too many details, just enough so that the interviewer understands the scenario.
T – Task: What were you doing and what was the goal?
A – Action: What you did specifically to achieve that goal. There is no ‘we’ in this section, just ‘I’.
R – Result: What was the outcome as a result of your performance? Try to include figures and statistics if you have them.

## Most Commonly Asked Behavioral Questions

Q. What was the most difficult decision you had to make?

Situation

The product manager was changing countries in the middle of our alpha preview of Database monitoring. We had meetings lined up with 8 Splunk O11y Cloud customers and he couldn't be available for the first 1 month.

Task

I had to coordinate with the engineering manager, the documentation writer, and our product marketing manager on who will be driving these meetings.

Action

Since I was closest to product from an end-to-end perspective, I ended up taking charge of meetings for the first half of the alpha preview. I wrote a script on how these recurring meetings would be handled to ensure these customers felt heard and were able to see the full advantage of the new feature that we were in the process of releasing. I had help from engineering manager for tasks which required technical finesse specifically around configuring our telemetry pipelines in the backend.

Result

We had a successful 2 month alpha preview which consisted of weekly recurring meetings with 8 Splunk O11y Cloud customers spanning a total of close to 60 hours.

Q. What are your greatest strengths? Weaknesses?

My greatest strength is being obsessed with technical details. I believe good developer experiences can only be designed by being well versed with the quirks of the technology keeping in line with the philosophy of bauhaus principles.

My greatest weakness is sometimes getting too caught up in technical details, which can slow down decision-making. I'm actively working on balancing attention to detail with efficiency.

Q. What was the most significant thing you accomplished in your most recent job?

Launching the database monitoring extension on Splunk O11y Cloud. This happened right after the Splunk acquisition. I had to learn a new product, a new design system, coordinate with a new design team, as well as build relationships with a brand new workstream. On top of that, database monitoring was the first extension built on top of Splunk O11y Cloud after the acquistion. All prior extensions were Splunk's own acquisitions.

Q. Why should we hire you?

I'm deeply interested in the developer tooling space. I have both an engineering and design background which specifically targets this market. I also have prior experience working at both early stage startups as well as large enterprises, which gives me a unique perspective on how to build products fast as well for scale.

Q. What are your salary requirements?

I'm looking for base cash compensation of $260k annually with a target total compensation of $400k annually. However, I'm open to discussing the full compensation package including equity, bonuses, and benefits.

Q. Describe the most significant or creative presentation you have had to complete.

A. I came up with the concept of composite components in Figma which urges all Figma artifacts to be comprised of nothing but components of various complexities. This also uses a noun-verb approach to define jobs which are then strung together to form workflows. This was presented to the entire design team last year and has seen a slow but favorable adoption.

Autotuning Kubernetes workloads for peak performance

## Addressing the gap and expanding capabilities

Splunk Observability Cloud excelled at application and infrastructure monitoring but lacked the end-to-end insight that database monitoring would provide. That gap forced users to switch tools, even as public forum requests and AppDynamics' $50M ARR success showed clear demand. Launching database monitoring would close the application-database performance divide and unlock a new DBA persona, expanding Splunk Observability Cloud's TAM.

In parallel, Splunk acquired Replex—renamed Application Optimization—for Kubernetes workload tuning that improves application performance. Integrating it into Splunk Observability Cloud added another optimization layer alongside the new database vertical.

![Extending capabilities at the intersection of applications and infrastructure](https://r2-image.raunaqgupta.workers.dev/dbmon-for-splunk-o11y-cloud/problem.png?f=avif)

## Designing for scalability

I supported two product and engineering teams each working independently within their respective domains by delivering designs that could scale across these new verticals while supporting future extensions. This included:

1. A new information architecture proposal,
2. Defining a taxonomy to establish new UI patterns,
3. Defining product strategy for releasing new beta features within the product,
4. In-product marketing to enable product-led adoption, and
5. Paving the way for future AI-assisted workflows.

## Impact

Alpha launch of Database monitoring had 11 multinational enterprise customers with a conversion rate of 64% within 3 months of launch. This number is currently estimated to grow to 25 by the end of Q1 2026.

## Solution

### Information architecture

![Information architecture utilizing the action-oriented UI states](https://r2-image.raunaqgupta.workers.dev/dbmon-for-splunk-o11y-cloud/ia.png?f=avif)

### Visualizations and micro-interactions

The query explain plan was visualized using a tree structure to represent the various operations involved in executing a database query. Micro-interactions were obsessed over to ensure that the tree structure was intuitive and easy to navigate.

![Constructing composite components in Figma](https://r2-image.raunaqgupta.workers.dev/dbmon-for-splunk-o11y-cloud/constructing-components.png?f=avif)

![Various states of the query explain plan component](https://r2-image.raunaqgupta.workers.dev/dbmon-for-splunk-o11y-cloud/queryExecutionPlan.component.png?f=avif)

### Defining AI-assisted workflows

I defined and designed AI-assisted workflows such as query summarization, and AI-based recommendations to help users optimize their database queries. Both these features are currently in customer preview and are getting positive feedback.

![AI-assisted query summarization and recommendations](https://r2-image.raunaqgupta.workers.dev/dbmon-for-splunk-o11y-cloud/query.preview.ai-recommendations.png?f=avif)
